No Schleswig-Holstein trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding survives in the record, so no division-specific divergence is documented for a visitor; documents and screening otherwise track the national position, with no division-specific border or document practice on file.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: The July 2026 prisoner-placement case (a court sent a person whose legal gender had been changed to a men's prison) turned state placement law into a national reform fight, and a March 2026 constitutional-law survey of the 2023-2026 reform wave, whose named statutes belong to other Land administrations, fed that fight. The region's government was one of five state governments that tabled a joint motion for a conversion-therapy ban presented in plenary in April 2019; the national ban was approved in May 2020.

No resident discrimination data or local surveys for the division survive in the record.

rewrites.summary:
This region is assessed at the national score: the dedicated country dossier identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02). A visitor stands under the national trans-equality law of 28 February 2023, which applies uniformly across the autonomous communities: adults rectify the registered sex marker by simple declaration with no medical diagnosis or treatment requirement and corresponding document adaptation, LGBTI non-discrimination protections extend to healthcare, employment and housing, and recognition from age 12 is available under conditions.

The regional base is permissive rather than restrictive: gender self-declaration has been possible since 2021, a gender-identity non-discrimination law has stood since 2014, and the region is listed among communities banning conversion therapies, so the national framework layers onto regional practice; parts of the region are named internationally known LGBT tourist destinations. For partner travel, the national law provides parental recognition for unmarried same-sex couples; no region-specific marriage provision is recorded.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: The comparative assessment is the dossier finding itself: no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02) was identified, so the region is scored with the parent nation. National-policy context: the 2023 law replaced a prior regime that required a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment for recognition, and the region was one of many communities that had already allowed self-declaration before that national reform. No litigation flux or comparison with neighbouring divisions is documented for this region in the dossier.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing instruments: the region created a same-sex couple registry in 2003, adopted an early regional law against gender-identity discrimination in 2014 that banned employment and other discrimination on gender-identity grounds and recognised trans persons' rights, and is listed among communities banning conversion therapies; the sex-marker rectification machinery operates on registered entries. No resident discrimination data or local surveys specific to the region is recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The sources are framework-level: the official gazette and an international human-rights organisation report the national law, and the encyclopaedia page supplies the only division-specific substance; no region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement series survives beyond those. No border-screening or visitor-document practice specific to the region is recorded, and the national document-adaptation provision, which applies to registered entries, is the only document-relevant item. The no-material-deviation finding is bounded by the ±0.02 threshold, and its absence is not proof of no local practice.

A visitor stands under the national trans-equality law of 28 February 2023: sex-marker rectification by simple declaration with no medical diagnosis or treatment requirement and corresponding document adaptation, LGBTI non-discrimination protections in healthcare, employment and housing, and recognition from age 12 under conditions; no region-specific law or incident series diverges from that national framework.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: National-policy context: the 2023 national law replaced a prior regime requiring a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment, and the region had already enacted its own gender-identity non-discrimination and trans-rights law in 2013, so the national reform layered onto existing regional protection rather than introducing it. The dossier finding compares this community with the neighbouring division of Navarra at the top of the per-capita offence table; no other comparison with neighbouring divisions is documented.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing content: the regional law against discrimination on grounds of gender identity and recognising trans persons' rights dates to 2013 and incorporated an LGTBI perspective into education and gender-violence prevention; a 2017 regional youth survey found 9 in 10 young residents favour same-sex marriage and legal sex change; the regional health service provided assisted reproduction regardless of sexual orientation; the regional government maintains an LGTBI public-order police force and an equality observatory with a comparative legislation database. Earlier institutional markers — a 1978 regional Pride march, the 1983 legalisation of an activist collective and the 1988 creation of a regional women's institute — are historical context rather than current legal facts.

rewrites.summary: Assessed materially in line with the national position. A visitor stands under the national trans-equality law of 28 February 2023, whose implementation — including its education-facing parts — falls to the regional government; the region's own statute prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or sex characteristics in public and private activity and bars any requirement to prove declared gender identity by psychological or medical report. No sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, so practical risk turns on the national victimisation baseline: a 2026 report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. Same-sex marriage has been legal nationally since 2 July 2005, the partner-travel baseline.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: National-framework context: the 2023 law replaced a prior national regime (a 2007 gender-identity law preceded it) that required diagnosis and treatment, and the region belongs to the first wave of regional LGTBI and trans-equality statutes approved in the 2010s. No litigation flux and no comparison with neighbouring divisions beyond the national framework is documented for this region.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-governing statute: the regional LGTBI-equality law of 27 May 2016 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or sex characteristics in public and private activity in the region, bars any requirement to prove declared gender identity by psychological or medical report, and creates a regional observatory; its sanctioning ladder fines minor breaches up to €3,000, serious breaches €3,001–€20,000 (including degrading remarks or incitement to violence against LGBTI persons), and very serious breaches €20,001–€45,000, with accessory penalties such as exclusion from regional public aid for up to one year, and multiple discrimination raises the infraction grade.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: No region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement finding beyond the sanctions statute was identified in the dossier, and no implementation detail is recorded for the national law's regional implementation. blindSourceSummaries: Official gazette text of the national law of 28 February 2023: applies uniformly across the autonomous communities of the parent nation, including this one; adults may rectify the registered sex marker by simple declaration, with no requirement of prior medical diagnosis or treatment and corresponding document adaptation; the law mandates public-policy, workplace, health and education measures, and its transitory provisions govern rectification applications pending at entry into force.

National-framework encyclopaedia page naming this state/province: among the first wave of regional LGTBI and trans-equality laws approved in the 2010s in eight regions; national framework dates — same-sex marriage legalised on 2 July 2005, a 2007 gender-identity law, and the 2023 trans-equality law whose implementation falls to the regional government.

Rectification of the registered sex entry proceeds by the person's freely expressed will (self-declaration), with no medical diagnosis or treatment requirement and corresponding document adaptation; the law provides protection and reparation against discrimination and violence, and recognition from age 12 is available under conditions; an international rights organisation ranked the nation among autonomy-first jurisdictions on the strength of the reform.
